title: A connected smooth finite covering of a semisimple group is semisimple
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Closed and normal subgroup schemes are as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. A semisimple group means a smooth connected affine group of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme; solvable means that successive derived subgroup schemes eventually become trivial, where the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. Let $f:G_1\to G_0$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of smooth connected groups with finite scheme-theoretic kernel. If $G_0$ is semisimple, then $G_1$ is semisimple. Here faithfully flat means that $F[G_1]$ is a faithfully flat $F[G_0]$-module, and finite kernel means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra; the kernel need not be reduced or central.

source.place: Lemma 19.14, printed p.400: for an isogeny G-prime to G, semisimplicity of G implies semisimplicity of G-prime. The proof uses the image of a smooth connected solvable normal subgroup of G-prime, which is trivial, so that subgroup is finite and hence trivial.

proof.text: Let $N\subseteq G_1$ be an arbitrary smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to $f|_N$ to write it as $N\xrightarrow{q} I\xrightarrow{j}G_0$, with $q$ faithfully flat and $j$ a closed immersion. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-image-geometry] hold for $f:G_1\to G_0$ and this factorization. Hence $I$ is a smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup of $G_0$.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400, image argument with solvable in place of unipotent.

proof.text: By the assumed semisimplicity of $G_0$, the subgroup $I$ is trivial. Consequently $f|_N$ equals the identity section of $G_0$ composed with $N\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. Thus $N$ factors through the scheme-theoretic kernel $K=\ker f$. This is scheme-theoretic factorization, not only a statement about rational points.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400, trivial image implies containment in the kernel.

proof.text: The inclusion $N\hookrightarrow K$ is closed: on the affine coordinate algebra $A=F[G_1]$, write the defining ideals as $J_N,J_K$. Factorization through $K$ says $J_K\subseteq J_N$, so $F[K]=A/J_K\to A/J_N=F[N]$ is surjective. This uses the affine characterization of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Since $F[K]$ is finite-dimensional over $F$, so is its quotient $B=F[N]$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400, finite-kernel step; affine closed-immersion calculation.

proof.text: Smoothness of $N/F$ gives reducedness of $B$ by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied to the sole fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Every descending chain of ideals of $B$ stabilizes because each strict inclusion decreases its finite $F$-vector-space dimension. Thus [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] writes $B$ as the finite product of its residue fields. Each factor is $F$ by clause 1 of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing], since $F$ is algebraically closed and $B$ is a finitely generated $F$-algebra. The identity section ensures this product is nonempty. Two or more factors would partition $\operatorname{Spec}B$ into two nonempty disjoint opens (use the coordinate idempotents); connectedness excludes this. There is exactly one factor, so $B\simeq F$ as an $F$-algebra.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400, finite smooth connected implies trivial; expanded using Stacks Tags 056T, 00J7 and 00JB and the affine Nullstellensatz.

proof.text: Therefore $N\simeq\operatorname{Spec}F$, and its group structure and inclusion are the trivial subgroup: the identity section is the unique $F$-morphism from $\operatorname{Spec}F$ to this $F$-scheme. As $N$ was arbitrary, $G_1$ has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup. The remaining conditions for semisimplicity of $G_1$ were hypotheses.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400, conclusion.
